your planner already knows how to do half of this

The Location list already offers Habits and Routines under "Or make it a". The second picture was taken by pressing that real control, not by painting the word in — so the pre-populating works today, and what is missing is the button that gets you there in one press.

One thing worth knowing: picking Habits converts the task into a habit rather than moving it, and it is refused if the task has no name yet. So the new button will create the item already named, or ask for the name first — otherwise pressing it would silently do nothing.

"whenever I press complete in the calendar I just don't want to see it in the calendar anymore - but I don't want it to come in a complete section within the setting, because routines and habits will never be complete unless I change the settings inside the edit."

2026-09-22, later "I'm referring to the million dollar routine — for some reason it looks like it's the only one where you click the three lines for the edit, it shows mark not complete instead of mark complete."

2026-09-22, round 3 "Number nine, you got it wrong. I'm referring to the task million dollar routine. And when I click the three dots, it doesn't show me the mark complete option. Fix that. It showed me mark incomplete."

how I would solve it

Reproduced, exactly as you described it. The menu label is decided by one line: node.done ? "Mark not complete" : "Complete". So that menu reads "Mark not complete" only when the routine is marked done forever — and that is what happened to this one.

There are two ways to complete a task, and they do not agree:
• the checkbox records that day — repeatDone: {"2026-09-22": true}, the routine itself untouched
• the three-dots menu does node.done = true, with no repeat check at all

So completing it once from the menu did not finish that day, it finished the routine — which is also why it disappeared from the tree. I would send the menu through the same per-day path as the checkbox, and clear the stuck flag on your existing item so its menu reads Complete again.

The picture shows: the three-dots menu on the Million dollar routine — the same row and the same menu in both pictures, so only the label changes
